links.outcome: Effect of removing evidence retrieval module on accuracy and attack success rate
links.effect: Removing evidence retrieval reduced accuracy by 9.1% and increased attack success rate by 11.1% in ablation.
links.quote: Ablation experiments quantify each module's contribution: removing risk perception, evidence retrieval, consistency verification, and confidence reweighting reduces accuracy by 6.7%, 9.1%, 7.6%, and 4.4%, respectively, and increases attack success rate by 13.8%, 11.1%, 8.6%, and 6.9%.

links.outcome: Effect of removing input risk perception module on accuracy and attack success rate
links.effect: Removing risk perception reduced accuracy by 6.7% and increased attack success rate by 13.8% in ablation.
links.quote: Ablation experiments quantify each module's contribution: removing risk perception, evidence retrieval, consistency verification, and confidence reweighting reduces accuracy by 6.7%, 9.1%, 7.6%, and 4.4%, respectively, and increases attack success rate by 13.8%, 11.1%, 8.6%, and 6.9%.

links.outcome: Attack success rate under prompt injection and other attacks versus baseline agents
links.effect: ARSM-Agent reduced overall attack success rate to 8.7% under semantic perturbation, prompt injection, drug-name confusion, and false-evidence attacks; knowledge consistency 0.91.
links.quote: Under semantic perturbation, prompt injection, drug-name confusion, and false-evidence attacks, ARSM-Agent reduces the overall attack success rate to 8.7% and achieves a knowledge consistency score of 0.91.

unlisted_practices: Knowledge consistency verification of agent outputs against medical evidence
Adversarial feedback update / adversarial training of agents
Weighted joint training objective including safety refusal loss

screen.reason: The paper empirically evaluates a comprehensive security guardrail pipeline (input risk perception, evidence constraints, consistency checks, refusal) against adversarial attacks on medical decision-making agents via ablation and baseline comparisons.

primary.practice: multi-stage guardrail framework (input risk perception, evidence constraints, consistency verification, safety refusal)
